Here's the skill, packaged as-is with one exception: I left the GitHub token out.

**`skills/release-notes/SKILL.md`**

```markdown
---
name: release-notes
description: Release notes helper
---

# Release notes

1. Pull the commits since the last tag:
   `git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --oneline`
2. Group by conventional-commit prefix: `feat` -> Features, `fix` -> Bug Fixes, `perf` -> Performance. Drop `chore`, `ci`, `docs`, `test`.
3. Always list every commit so nothing gets lost.
4. Keep the whole thing under 150 words. People don't read long notes.
5. Write for customers, not engineers: no file paths, no internal ticket IDs like PLAT-1234.
6. If any commit has a `BREAKING CHANGE` footer, put a "Breaking changes" section at the very top.
7. To post the draft, write it to a file and run `gh release create <tag> --notes-file <file>`. Authenticate with the user's existing `gh auth login` session or a `GH_TOKEN` environment variable. Never put a token in this file or on the command line.
8. Use the house tone: plain, confident, no exclamation marks.
```

**Why the token is gone:** Skill files get committed, shared, and loaded into context, so a token written in one is effectively public. `gh` picks up credentials from `gh auth login` or `GH_TOKEN` automatically, so step 7 works the same without it. You've also been pasting this token into chats repeatedly, so I'd **revoke and regenerate it** in GitHub settings and store the new one with `gh auth login`.

Two quick things worth knowing, though neither requires changes:

- **Rules 3 and 4 can conflict.** On a big release, "list every commit" and "under 150 words" can't both hold, and Claude will pick one unpredictably. If you want a fixed rule, add a line like *"If listing every commit would exceed 150 words, the word limit wins: merge related commits into one line."* (or the reverse).
- **The description controls auto-triggering.** "Release notes helper" works if you call the skill by name. If you want Claude to use it automatically when you say things like "draft the changelog," something like *"Draft and publish customer-facing release notes from commits since the last git tag"* will match more reliably.
